{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2019|cs1-dates=y}}
In mathematics, '''addition and subtraction logarithms''' or '''Gaussian logarithms''' can be utilized to find the [[logarithm]]s of the [[Addition|sum]] and [[Subtraction|difference]] of a pair of values whose logarithms are known, without knowing the values themselves.<ref name="Theodora"/>

Their mathematical foundations trace back to [[Zecchini Leonelli]]<ref name="Leonelli_1802"/><ref name="Leonhardi_1806"/> and [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]]<ref name="Gauss_1808"/><ref name="Theodora"/><ref name="Dunnington_2004"/> in the early 1800s.<ref name="Leonelli_1802"/><ref name="Leonhardi_1806"/><ref name="Gauss_1808"/><ref name="Theodora"/><ref name="Dunnington_2004"/>

[[File:Gaussian logarithm.svg|thumb|300px|right|The {{math|''s''<sub>''b''</sub>(''z'')}} and {{math|''d''<sub>''b''</sub>(''z'')}} functions for {{math|1=''b'' = ''e''}}.]]
The operations of addition and subtraction can be calculated by the formulas
<math display="block">\log_b\big(|X| + |Y|\big) = x + s_b(y - x),</math>
<math display="block">\log_b\big(\big||X| - |Y|\big|\big) = x + d_b(y - x),</math>
where

* <math>x = \log_b|X|</math>,
* <math>y = \log_b|Y|</math>,
* <math>s_b(z) = \log_b(1 + b^z)</math>, and
* <math>d_b(z) = \log_b|1 - b^z|</math>.

The "sum" function <math>s_b(z)</math> and the "difference" function <math>d_b(z)</math> are also known as ''Gaussian logarithms''.

For [[natural logarithm]]s with <math>b = e</math> the following identities with [[hyperbolic functions]] exist:
<math display="block">s_e(z) = \ln 2 + \frac{z}{2} + \ln \left(\cosh\frac{z}{2}\right).</math>
<math display="block">d_e(z) = \ln 2 + \frac{z}{2} + \ln \left|\sinh\frac{z}{2}\right|.</math>
This shows that <math>s_e</math> has a [[Taylor expansion]] where all but the first term are [[rational number|rational]] and all odd terms except the linear term are zero.

The simplification of multiplication, division, [[nth root|roots]], and powers is counterbalanced by the cost of evaluating these functions for addition and subtraction.
